mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has risen monotonically from -30.9% to -24.3% over four weeks, indicating a consistent recovery trend. This momentum will persist over the next four weeks, driving RETAIL_REC further above the current baseline mean of -27.3%.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improved 6.6 percentage points from t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days does not exceed the mean of the last 28 days (-27.3%), or reverses by more than 3 percentage points week-on-week.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT mobility has stabilized near -34.7% over the past two weeks after declining from -41.6%. This stabilization signals commuter confidence recovery. When TRANSIT stabilizes within a 2-point band for two consecutive weeks, retail footfall follows within one week as workers resume shopping routines.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT week-on-week change falls within ±2 percentage points for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT at -36.0% (t-1w) and -34.7% (t-0w), change of 1.3 points
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase within one week of TRANSIT stabilization, or TRANSIT resumes declining by more than 2 points in the following week.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility has declined from -31.1% to -32.3% over four weeks, indicating weakening office attendance. This contraction suppresses retail footfall because fewer workers commute past retail zones. RETAIL_REC will decline over the next four weeks as WORKPLACES weakness persists.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES falls below -32% for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES declined 1.2 points from t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days exceeds the last 28-day mean, or WORKPLACES recovers by more than 2 percentage points in any single week.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility has remained negative and stable (-12.7% to -6.9%) while RESIDENTIAL has remained elevated (10.6% to 8.3%). This persistent home-bias combined with weak outdoor activity signals low consumer mobility appetite. The interaction of elevated RESIDENTIAL and suppressed PARKS indicates consumers are not yet ready to venture into retail zones; RETAIL_REC will remain depressed.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL remains above 8% AND PARKS remains below -5% simultaneously
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL at 8.3% and PARKS at -6.9% at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases by more than 2 percentage points over the next two weeks, or PARKS rises above 0% while RESIDENTIAL falls below 8%.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM has remained stable at -8% to -10% over four weeks, indicating essential shopping is constrained by policy or capacity limits. When essential shopping is suppressed, discretionary retail (RETAIL_REC) is also suppressed through the same underlying policy regime. RETAIL_REC will remain depressed as long as GROCERY_PHARM stays below -8%.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM remains below -8% for three consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM at -8.4% at t-0w, stable range -8.1% to -10.6%
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days exceeds the last 28-day mean while GROCERY_PHARM remains below -8%, or GROCERY_PHARM rises above -7% without corresponding RETAIL_REC increase.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES have both improved from their t-3w lows (-41.6% and -31.1% respectively) to t-0w levels (-34.7% and -32.3%). The joint recovery of commuting infrastructure and workplace attendance creates a multiplier effect: more workers commuting means more retail exposure. RETAIL_REC will accelerate upward when both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES improve simultaneously.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both improve week-on-week by at least 1 percentage point in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved 6.9 points from t-3w to t-0w; WORKPLACES declined 1.2 points
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase within two weeks of synchronized TRANSIT and WORKPLACES improvement, or either series reverses by more than 2 points.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility has been negative throughout the observation window (-12.7% to -6.9%), suggesting winter weather suppression of outdoor activity. As February progresses toward spring (March-April), PARKS mobility will recover. This outdoor activity recovery signals seasonal behavioral shift that precedes retail recovery by one week, as consumers transition from home-bound to mobile.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises above -3% for one week, indicating seasonal transition onset
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS improved 5.8 points from t-3w to t-0w, trend toward positive
failure_condition: PARKS does not rise above -3% within the next four weeks, or RETAIL_REC does not increase within one week of PARKS crossing -3%.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL elevation (8-10%) combined with TRANSIT suppression (-34 to -41%) indicates a regime where people work from home and avoid transit. This regime suppresses RETAIL_REC because home-workers do not pass through retail zones during commutes. RETAIL_REC will only recover when RESIDENTIAL falls below 9% AND TRANSIT rises above -33% simultaneously, signaling return to office-based work.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL remains above 9% OR TRANSIT remains below -33% for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL at 8.3% and TRANSIT at -34.7% at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days exceeds the last 28-day mean while RESIDENTIAL stays above 9% and TRANSIT stays below -33%.
